editorial:
Imagine stepping back into the mid-70s for a bright, colorful musical celebration that feels like a giant party. You get to follow the amazing Sofia Rotaru and the Chervona Ruta ensemble as they bring a mix of Ukrainian, Romanian, and Russian sounds to life. The vibe is purely joyful and light, focusing more on the magic of performance than a heavy plot. With the Kyiv Music Hall ballet and the Smerechyna dance group joining in, you will see some incredible choreography and costumes that make the whole screen pop with energy.

What really stands out is the raw talent of the singers and the upbeat energy of the dance numbers. Since it is a TV movie from 1975, the pacing is slower than modern films, but the music keeps you moving. If you love old-school variety shows or global folk music, you will adore this. It is a great piece of history to experience.
endingExplained: The film wraps up with a grand final performance that brings all the musical groups together for one last big show. There is no shocking twist here because it is a celebratory musical. Instead, it ends on a high note of unity and art. You see the performers bowing to the crowd, leaving you with a feeling of happiness and a deep appreciation for the diverse cultures and languages shared throughout the movie.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves folk music and old-school dance performances.
